alerts.explanation: The browser identity changed mid-session from 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36' to 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:121.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/121.0', which may mean the cookie is being used from another device; can also be an innocent browser update.

cookieFixes: Enable the Secure flag so the cookie only travels over HTTPS and cannot be sniffed.
Enable the HttpOnly flag so JavaScript cannot read the cookie, which limits theft by cross-site scripting.
Set SameSite to Strict or Lax so other sites cannot trigger requests with the cookie.

alerts.explanation: Cookie security vulnerability: Secure flag missing: cookie can be sent over unencrypted connections and sniffed; HttpOnly missing: JavaScript can read the cookie, so cross-site scripting could steal it; SameSite None: cookie is sent on cross-site requests, which helps cross-site request forgery
alerts.recommendation: Configure session cookies with: Secure=true, HttpOnly=true, SameSite=Strict or Lax
